claim: Willis Tower Skydeck 2026 general admission is $32 adult (12+), $24 youth (3-11), under 3 free; Expedited Entry from $55; open daily 9am-10pm (Sat from 8:30am), last entry 30 min before close.
quote: Adults (ages 12+): Starting at $32 ... Youth (ages 3-11): Starting at $24 ... Expedited Entry: Starting at $55 ... Summer hours (May 26 - September 30): 9:00am - 10:00pm ... Saturday: 8:30am - 10:00pm ... Last entry 30 minutes prior to close

claim: 360 Chicago observation deck (94th floor, formerly John Hancock) 2026 admission is $30 weekday / $35 weekend adult, youth from $20; TILT add-on is +$9-10; open daily 9am-11pm with last entry 10pm.
quote: Weekday adult tickets cost $30; weekend tickets are $35. Youth tickets start at $20 ... TILT costs an additional $9-10 ... Open daily 9 am-11 pm; last entry 10 pm.

claim: Millennium Park including Cloud Gate (The Bean) is free and open daily 6am-11pm; the campus also has Crown Fountain, gardens, and free Pritzker Pavilion concerts.
quote: Cloud Gate and all of Millennium Park is completely free and open to the public daily from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. ... the iconic Cloud Gate statue (aka "The Bean"), interactive fountains, tranquil gardens, free events, public art

claim: Adjacent Maggie Daley Park is free and features a fantasy Play Garden, a 40-foot climbing wall, and an 18-hole mini-golf course, oriented toward families.
quote: Maggie Daley Park is a kid's fantasyland with the Play Garden ... featuring suspension bridges, tube slides, and a big ship to explore, while older kids flock to the 40-foot climbing wall and 18-hole mini golf course.

claim: Navy Pier entry is free; the Centennial Wheel (~200 ft, climate-controlled gondolas, ~13-15 min ride) costs roughly $25 incl. fees, with hours varying (Fri/Sat to 9pm, weekdays to 8pm, Sun to 7pm).
quote: soaring nearly 200 feet and providing 360-degree panoramic views ... climate-controlled gondolas ... A standard ride typically lasts 13-15 minutes ... there is no admission fee to enter Navy Pier itself ... General admission starts at $24.72 per person (including fees)

claim: Buckingham Fountain in Grant Park is free, runs early May-mid October, with a 20-minute major water display every hour on the hour (center jet to 150 ft) and a light-and-music show at dusk; new seating added for 2026.
quote: produces a major water display for 20 minutes every hour ... a center jet shoots water to a height of 150 feet ... Beginning at dusk, a spectacular light and music display ... New for 2026, seating will be available around the fountain beginning May 30.

claim: Skydeck (103rd floor, 1,353 ft) features The Ledge glass balconies extending 4.3 ft out, with west/river views; 360 Chicago (94th, ~1,000 ft) has TILT and is widely cited as having better lake and city views with shorter waits.
quote: Skydeck is located on the 103rd floor of Willis Tower at 1,353 feet ... The Ledge, five glass balconies extending 4.3 feet ... 360 Chicago offers TILT ... 360 Chicago tends to have shorter wait times compared to Willis Tower.

claim: Reddit/local consensus: The Bean is a worthwhile quick free stop; Willis Skydeck is seen by some locals as overpriced; Navy Pier is called a tourist trap ("shops out on the lake") best for evening fireworks, with the Riverwalk recommended as an alternative.
quote: It is not a good value. It is sensationalized to the point of ridiculousness ... just a bunch of shops out on the lake ... navy pier's beer garden on Saturday during the summer is kind of a hidden gem ... the Riverwalk as an alternative
